source.section: Form N-11 lines 7-12, 19-20 and 23-27 (pages 2-3); PDF page 11 (Line 7), PDF page 20 (Line 23 standard deduction table, Line 25 exemptions), PDF page 9 (Lines 6a, 6b, 'age 65 or over as of January 1, 2026'), PDF page 20 (Line 27 Tax Table), PDF page 50 (2025 Tax Rate Schedules)

worked: Married filing jointly, 66 and 63: only the older spouse is 65 or over (each person's own age counts, lines 6a and 6b), so one age-65 exemption, not two. Wages 90,000 earned by the younger spouse, interest 5,000. Line 7 federal AGI = wages 90,000.00 (younger spouse) + interest 5,000.00 = 95,000.00. Federal taxable income = 95,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age-65 addition = 61,900.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 11 total additions = 0.00; line 12 = 95,000.00 + 0.00 = 95,000.00. Line 19 total subtractions = 0.00; line 20 Hawaii AGI = 95,000.00 - 0.00 = 95,000.00. Line 23 standard deduction (married filing jointly, PDF page 20 table) 8,800.00; line 24 = 95,000.00 - 8,800.00 = 86,200.00. Line 6e exemptions: 2 regular + 1 age 65 or over = 3; line 25 = 3 x 1,144.00 = 3,432.00. Line 26 taxable income = 86,200.00 - 3,432.00 = 82,768.00. Line 27 tax, Schedule II (PDF page 50) as bands on 82,768.00: 19,200.00 x 1.4% = 268.80; 9,600.00 x 3.2% = 307.20; 9,600.00 x 5.5% = 528.00; 9,600.00 x 6.4% = 614.40; 24,000.00 x 6.8% = 1,632.00; 10,768.00 x 7.2% = 775.296; sum = 4,125.696, to the cent 4,125.70; tax = 4,125.70 (Form N-11 line 27 uses the Tax Table below 100,000 of taxable income (PDF page 20, Line 27): the table row 82,750 to 82,800 gives 4,126; this case uses the bands as numbers). No credits modelled (refundable food/excise and renters credits, lines 28-29, not claimed): state income tax = 4,125.70.
